messages:
anya: quick SRE check — we're proposing to tighten per-route quotas for /v1/generate and change soft-429 semantics. quick notes: - per-route bucket -> 60 req/min default (was 120) - allow short bursts up to 10 reqs in 1s (token burst) - clients should see 429 w/ headers and still receive partial body for structured errors

mike: is this change for Hosted only or Dedicated too?

anya: hosted only for now. Dedicated will be opt-in via config. want to minimize surprise for customers.

sowmya: compatibility question — are we changing retry headers? currently we return `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.

anya: keeping `Retry-After` for hard 429. adding `X-RW-Quota-Remaining` and `X-RW-Quota-Bucket` for visibility. no changes to `X-RateLimit-Reset` right now.

jess: can we see an example 429 response body? SDKs parse body to decide backoff vs degrade.

anya: sure — thinking something like:

```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RW-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-RW-Quota-Bucket: generate:v1:user:default
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_exceeded",
    "message": "per-route quota exceeded",
    "soft": true,
    "hint": "consider reducing concurrency or using fallback model"
  }
}
```

mike: note the `soft` flag — how do we define it? soft=true means we still return partial output for streaming requests?

anya: proposal: soft=true => not catastrophic — we may return a short partial stream or a deterministic cutoff token. hard 429 => no content / user must retry.

rahul: SDK impact: we currently treat any 429 as retry with exponential backoff. need to update to check error.soft and maybe degrade to lower-capacity model automatically.

sowmya: agree — need guidance doc for SDKs. Also: will we add a per-route header for burst allowance? i.e., current bucket refill/speed isn't exposed.

anya: adding `X-RW-Burst-Allowance: 10` to responses when applicable. it will be dynamic (client can peek to know if next few requests will likely be allowed).

tim: timeline? I can update runtime once API plan is final. need at least 2 weeks for rollout + canary.

anya: target: canary next Tues, full rollout in 2 weeks after canary if no regressions.

deploy-bot: infra: canary rollout scheduled for 2024-10-10T14:00Z, 5% traffic for 6h.

jess: tests: we'll add an integration that mocks concurrent clients to validate burst behavior + header correctness.

rahul: will alerting change? SRE needs new pagers for unexpected hard 429 spikes.

anya: yes — create a paging rule for spike in hard 429 rate > 1% of requests in 5m.

mike: small nit: header name `X-RW-Quota-Remaining` — prefer singular `X-RW-Quota-Remaining` ok, just confirming format (int). also ensure TTL in seconds.

anya: good call. it's an integer remaining tokens, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` stays epoch seconds for the window end.

sowmya: SDK owners: please add logic to treat soft=true as degrade path: fallback to next model and do jittered backoff. We can publish snippet in docs.

jess: will do. also adding a lint check that headers exist on 429 responses for all paths.

tim: runtime detail — KV cache flush behavior on soft 429s? we should keep KV cache intact so subsequent retries don't restart context.

anya: agreed. KV cache should be preserved; only truncate the outgoing stream where needed.

mike: one more: per-route config UI needs a tooltip explaining burst vs sustained rate.

anya: UX will add that. ok action items: - tim: implement header plumbing + burst allowance (due Thu) - jess: integration tests + lint check (due Fri) - rahul: pager + dashboard for hard 429 spikes (due Mon) - sowmya: SDK guidance + code sample (due Fri) - mike: update docs & console tooltip (due next Wed)

anya: ping me on PRs, will hold a 15m async review window tomorrow 9am PT. thanks :thumbsup:

mike: ack

sowmya: ack

jess: ack

rahul: ack

tim: ack

rate-bot: reminder: API contract change requires 7-day deprecation notice for existing customers. Please confirm.

anya: good catch — we'll post deprecation notice today and include migration steps.

mike: can we add a header `X-RW-Soft-429` (boolean) to make it simpler for older SDKs that don't parse body?

sowmya: prefer `X-RW-Soft-429: 1` rather than boolean string. less parsing surprises.

anya: ok final decision: add `X-RW-Soft-429: 1` for soft cases, keep body soft flag as well.

jess: I'll make tests check both header and body.

anya: great. closing this thread — will open PRs against runtime + docs and tag the SDK teams. cheers!
